text: Hello! Pip. I play at these tables most days, and I lose at them most days.
Do you know the game? Doesn't matter. Sit down, I'll show you the first rule.
Is that a board? Nobody carries a board down this street.
Pip. Where did you get it?

choices.text: It was in my room. I don't know what it is.

text: You don't know what it IS. Sit down. This is the best thing to happen to me all month.
It's Go. Black and white, we take turns putting stones on the crossings. I'll show you the rest by playing.
One rule for now. A stone needs an empty crossing beside it, or it comes off the board.
Take one of mine and you win. Seven by seven. Ready?
Stones don't move once they're down. Each one needs an empty crossing next to it to breathe.
Fill the last one and it comes off. Take one of mine and you've won.
Back for more? Good.
Quick one? Nine by nine, nothing counts, and I'll try a ladder.
Right! I'm here most days. Losing.
Another?
You took one! First game. That's the engine of it, right there: count the breaths, get there first.
Go down to De Ketel, three steps under the kettle sign. Ask for Wren. She teaches the rest.
Got you! Don't mind that, I've had three years of practice at exactly this.
Go down to De Ketel, three steps under the kettle sign. Ask for Wren. She teaches the rest properly.
Lost again. I'm not being polite, I enjoy it. The ladder didn't work, did it.
Bertie says it never works. One day.
I WON. The ladder worked! Did you see it work?
Don't tell Bertie. He'll say it was luck, and it was.
